# Step 1: Create a GitHub Account

If you don't already have one:

1. Go to [github.com](https://github.com) and click **"Sign Up"**
2. Use your **NIEHS email** — this gives institutional recognition
3. Choose a **professional username** (e.g., `jsmith-niehs`)
4. Complete email verification
5. Skip the personalization steps for now

> **Tip:** NIH employees may qualify for a free GitHub Education/Research plan,
> which includes unlimited private repos, CI minutes, and Copilot access.


# Step 1b: Create Your First Repository

1. Click the green **"New"** button (or go to [github.com/new](https://github.com/new))
2. **Repository name:** `git-workshop` (short, lowercase, hyphens not spaces)
3. **Description:** "Practice repo for NIEHS Git training"
4. **Visibility:** Private (you can make it public later)
5. **Check** "Add a README file"
6. **Add .gitignore:** select **"R"** from the dropdown
7. **License:** skip for now (we'll cover licensing later)
8. Click **"Create repository"**

You now have a repository with a README.md and an R-specific .gitignore!


# Step 2: Create a Personal Access Token (PAT)

GitHub no longer accepts passwords for Git operations. You need a Personal
Access Token (PAT) instead.

## What is a PAT?

A PAT is a long string of characters that acts as your password when Git talks
to GitHub. It's more secure than a password because:

- You control exactly what permissions it has (scopes)
- You set an expiration date
- You can revoke it anytime without changing your GitHub password

## Creating the PAT

1. **GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic)**
   - Quick link: [github.com/settings/tokens](https://github.com/settings/tokens)
2. Click **"Generate new token"** → **"Generate new token (classic)"**
3. **Note:** `Posit Cloud access`
4. **Expiration:** 90 days (or custom — you can always regenerate)
5. **Scopes:** check **"repo"** (full control of private repositories)
6. Click **"Generate token"**

**⚠️ COPY THE TOKEN NOW — you will never see it again after leaving this page!**

## Understanding PAT Scopes

| Scope | Description | Need it? |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| **repo** | Read/write access to repositories | **Yes** |
| workflow | Update GitHub Actions workflows | No |
| write:packages | Upload packages to GitHub Packages | No |
| read:org | Read organization membership | No |
| gist | Create gists (code snippets) | No |

For this workshop, **"repo" is the only scope you need.** Principle of least
privilege: only grant what you actually use.

## Where to Store Your PAT

- **Password manager** (1Password, Bitwarden, etc.) — recommended
- **A secure note** — acceptable for today
- **NOT** in a file in your project, NOT in your code, NOT in a sticky note

<div style="padding: 12px; background-color: #FEE2E2; border-left: 4px solid #DC2626; margin: 16px 0;">
**Warning:** Your PAT is as powerful as your password. If someone gets your PAT,
they can access your repositories. Treat it like a password.
</div>


# Step 3: Create a Posit Cloud Project from GitHub

1. Log in at [posit.cloud](https://posit.cloud)
2. Click **"New Project"** dropdown → **"New Project from Git Repository"**
3. Paste the **HTTPS URL** from your GitHub repo
   - Go to your repo on GitHub → click the green **"Code"** button → copy the HTTPS URL
   - It looks like: `https://github.com/yourusername/git-workshop.git`
   - ⚠️ **Use HTTPS, not SSH** — SSH requires extra setup on Posit Cloud
4. Wait for the project to build (30–60 seconds)
5. You should see your files (README.md, .gitignore) in the Files pane

## HTTPS vs. SSH on Posit Cloud

| | **HTTPS + PAT** ✓ | **SSH Keys** |
|---|---|---|
| Setup | Works out of the box | Requires key pair generation |
| URL format | `https://github.com/...` | `git@github.com:...` |
| Authentication | Username + PAT when prompted | SSH key exchange |
| Credential cache | 12 hours on Posit Cloud | Permanent until key revoked |
| From "New Project" | Yes | No (HTTPS only for cloning) |

**We use HTTPS + PAT for this workshop.** It's simpler and works immediately.


# Step 4: Configure Your Git Identity

Open the **Terminal** tab (bottom-left pane → Terminal) and type:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@niehs.nih.gov"
```

Verify with:

```bash
git config --global --list
```

You should see your name and email listed.

### Why this matters

Every commit you make is labeled with your name and email. This is how Git
(and your collaborators) know who made each change. Use your real name and
your NIEHS email so your contributions are properly attributed.

### Posit Cloud specifics

- The **credential cache** is set to 12 hours by default — you typically enter
  your PAT once per session
- When prompted for a **"password"**, enter your **PAT** — not your GitHub password
- If you linked your GitHub account to Posit Cloud during signup, your
  name/email may already be configured

# Alternative: Enable Git on an Existing Project

If you already have a Posit Cloud project without Git:

**Via the RStudio menu:**

```
Tools → Version Control → Project Setup → Version Control System → Git → Yes
```

<div style="padding: 12px; background-color: #FEE2E2; border-left: 4px solid #DC2626; margin: 16px 0;">
**Important:** `usethis::use_git()` does **NOT** work on Posit Cloud. You must
use the menu method above.
</div>

Then connect to GitHub via the Terminal:

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourusername/repo-name.git
git push -u origin main
# Enter username + PAT when prompted
```


# Exercise 0: Verify Your Setup {.unnumbered}

Run through this checklist in the **Terminal** (not the Console):

```bash
# 1. Can you see the Git tab in the upper-right pane? (Yes/No)

# 2. Check your identity
git config --global user.name
git config --global user.email

# 3. Check repo status
git status
# Should say: "On branch main" and "nothing to commit"

# 4. Check remote connection
git remote -v
# Should show your GitHub URL for "origin"

# 5. Check Git version
git --version
```

If anything looks wrong, raise your hand — we'll troubleshoot together.

**Common issues:**

- "Not a git repository" → You may have opened the Console instead of the
  Terminal, or the project wasn't created from a Git repo
- No user.name/email → Run the `git config` commands from Step 4
- No remote → Run `git remote add origin <your-URL>`
